title: The image presheaf of a map that is surjective after sheafification has the same sheafification
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $\varphi:F\to G$ a morphism of presheaves of sets on $\mathcal C$. Let $G'\subseteq G$ be its image presheaf, $G'(U)=\varphi_U(F(U))$ with the restriction maps of $G$, and $\iota:G'\to G$ the inclusion, so that $\varphi=\iota\circ\psi$ with $\psi:F\to G'$ surjective on sections over every object. Assume that $\varphi$ becomes surjective after sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]: for every object $U$ and every $t\in G^\#(U)$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}_{i}$ such that each $t|_{U_i}$ lies in the image of $\varphi^\#_{U_i}:F^\#(U_i)\to G^\#(U_i)$. Then (a) $\varphi$ is locally surjective: for every object $U$ and $g\in G(U)$ there are a covering $\{U_i\to U\}_i$ and $f_i\in F(U_i)$ with $\varphi(f_i)=g|_{U_i}$; and (b) $\iota^\#:G'^\#\to G^\#$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of sets.

proof.text: Notation and functoriality. Write $\theta_F:F\to F^\#$, $\theta_G:G\to G^\#$, $\theta_{G'}:G'\to G'^\#$ for the canonical maps of the sheafifications [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For a morphism of presheaves $\alpha:P\to Q$, $\alpha^\#:P^\#\to Q^\#$ is by the universal property the unique morphism of sheaves with $\alpha^\#\circ\theta_P=\theta_Q\circ\alpha$; uniqueness gives $(\beta\circ\alpha)^\#=\beta^\#\circ\alpha^\#$. In particular $\varphi^\#\circ\theta_F=\theta_G\circ\varphi$ and, from $\varphi=\iota\circ\psi$, $\varphi^\#=\iota^\#\circ\psi^\#$. All of these are morphisms of presheaves, so they commute with restriction along every morphism of $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Sites, Section 00W1 (sheafification), the functoriality of F -> F^#, Lemma Tag 00WJ (label lemma-sheafification-exact) statement

proof.text: (a), first half: local lifts in $F$ of the image of $g$ in $G^\#$. Let $U$ be an object and $g\in G(U)$; put $t=\theta_G(g)\in G^\#(U)$. By hypothesis there are a covering $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ and $x_i\in F^\#(U_i)$ with $\varphi^\#(x_i)=t|_{U_i}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] (first assertion, for the presheaf $F$ and the section $x_i$) there are, for each $i$, a covering $\{U_{ij}\to U_i\}_{j\in J_i}$ and $f_{ij}\in F(U_{ij})$ with $x_i|_{U_{ij}}=\theta_F(f_{ij})$. Then, by step 1, $\theta_G(\varphi(f_{ij}))=\varphi^\#(\theta_F(f_{ij}))=\varphi^\#(x_i)|_{U_{ij}}=t|_{U_{ij}}=\theta_G(g|_{U_{ij}})$ in $G^\#(U_{ij})$.

source.place: Sites, Lemma Tag 00WK (label lemma-sections-sheafification), assertion (1), applied to F; Definition Tag 00WM (label definition-sheaves-injective-surjective) (2) for the hypothesis

proof.text: (a), second half: from equality in $G^\#$ to equality on a covering in $G$. The sections $\varphi(f_{ij})$ and $g|_{U_{ij}}$ of $G(U_{ij})$ have the same image in $G^\#(U_{ij})$ (step 2), so by the last assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] (for the presheaf $G$) there is a covering $\{U_{ijk}\to U_{ij}\}_{k\in K_{ij}}$ with $\varphi(f_{ij})|_{U_{ijk}}=g|_{U_{ijk}}$. Put $f_{ijk}=f_{ij}|_{U_{ijk}}\in F(U_{ijk})$; as $\varphi$ is a morphism of presheaves, $\varphi(f_{ijk})=\varphi(f_{ij})|_{U_{ijk}}=g|_{U_{ijk}}$. By axiom (ii) of a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], applied twice, $\{U_{ijk}\to U\}_{i,j,k}$ (the composites $U_{ijk}\to U_{ij}\to U_i\to U$) is a covering of $U$. This is (a).

source.place: Sites, Lemma Tag 00WK (label lemma-sections-sheafification), the uniqueness in its converse, applied to G; Definition Tag 00VH (label definition-site) axiom (2)

proof.text: (b), $\iota^\#$ is a monomorphism of $\Sh(\mathcal C)$. Each $\iota_U:G'(U)\to G(U)$ is an inclusion, so $\iota$ is a monomorphism of presheaves of sets (if $\iota\circ a=\iota\circ b$ then $a_U=b_U$ for every $U$). Equivalently the commutative square with sides $\mathrm{id}_{G'},\mathrm{id}_{G'}$ and $\iota,\iota$ is a fibre product square $G'=G'\times_GG'$ in presheaves. Sheafification commutes with finite limits [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact] (the site has a set of objects and morphisms by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]), so the square with sides $\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id}$ and $\iota^\#,\iota^\#$ is a fibre product square in $\Sh(\mathcal C)$. Hence $\iota^\#$ is a monomorphism: if $a,b:\mathcal T\to G'^\#$ satisfy $\iota^\#a=\iota^\#b$, the induced $c:\mathcal T\to G'^\#$ with $\mathrm{id}\circ c=a$ and $\mathrm{id}\circ c=b$ gives $a=c=b$.

(b), $\iota^\#$ is an epimorphism of $\Sh(\mathcal C)$. The hypothesis says that the morphism of sheaves $\varphi^\#:F^\#\to G^\#$ is surjective in the sense of sheaves, so it is an epimorphism of $\Sh(\mathcal C)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective]. If $a,b:G^\#\to\mathcal H$ are morphisms of sheaves with $a\circ\iota^\#=b\circ\iota^\#$, then $a\circ\varphi^\#=a\circ\iota^\#\circ\psi^\#=b\circ\iota^\#\circ\psi^\#=b\circ\varphi^\#$ by step 1, hence $a=b$.

source.place: Sites, Lemma Tag 00WN (label lemma-mono-epi-sheaves), surjective = epimorphism

proof.text: (b), conclusion. By steps 4 and 5, $\iota^\#:G'^\#\to G^\#$ is both a monomorphism and an epimorphism of $\Sh(\mathcal C)$, hence an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-sets-mono-epi-iso].
